title: Introduce onboarding epoch, size-aware profile rollforward, and autorelease teasers
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Adds 'epoch' grouping for onboarding, a size-aware rollforward policy that biases initial rollouts toward lower-footprint variants, and an automated release-teaser generator that drafts concise changelog snippets from sampled perf deltas and metadata. Includes migrations, feature flag, tests. Backfill strategy and rollback plan included.
description:
Motivation: Onboarding churn and noisy changelogs make staged rollouts and release summaries manual and error-prone. This change introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) an onboarding 'epoch' concept (immutable lifecycle batch id) to let teams reason about staged rollforwards and opt-in rollbacks; 2) a size-aware rollforward heuristic that prefers lower-memory/quantized variants for initial traffic to reduce cost/risk; 3) an autorelease-teaser generator that synthesizes short human-editable changelog blurbs based on sampled performance deltas, profile diffs, and risk tags.

What I changed (high level): added epoch_id to model manifests and registry APIs, a migration to backfill epoch for active models using intake timestamp heuristics, a new rollforward policy implementation with configurable weights (latency/cost/quality/size), a teaser generator service that emits compact draft snippets saved to release_drafts/<model>/<epoch>.json (human-editable), and a feature flag (feature.onboard.epoch_autorelease) gating the auto-draft behavior.

Why this design: epoch grouping keeps release metadata immutable and simplifies rollback decisions (rollbacks can reference an epoch id). The size-aware rollforward mitigates first-wave OOMs and helps customers get predictions with lower unit cost while we monitor quality. Draft teasers reduce the friction for PMs and docs to create release notes and are intentionally conservative (only surface deltas above configured thresholds).

Backward compatibility & rollout: all new fields are optional. Existing manifests without epoch_id are backfilled by a one-off job in this PR; the code tolerates missing values. The feature flag defaults to off in production; rollout plan: deploy to staging, enable feature for internal teams, run backfill, monitor SLOs for 48h, then flip on for self-serve orgs.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for rollforward scoring, end-to-end tests for teaser generation using synthetic perf traces, migration dry-run output, and integration tests for API surfaces. Benchmarked the policy decision overhead (sub-millisecond per decision) and included stress test harness results in the PR artifacts.

Operational notes: teasers include an anonymized sample of metrics (no PII), a confidence bucket, and a recommended human-friendly blurb. We store drafts in the model registry with metadata to trace which profile samples informed the teaser. The teaser generator can be re-run deterministically with the same seed to reproduce drafts.

Rollback plan: the epoch abstraction makes rollbacks explicit by reverting to a prior epoch id. If the teaser generator is noisy, feature flag can be disabled and drafts deleted; the migration has a reversible dry-run to restore previous state.

Links: Linear ENG-3421; internal spec: docs/onboard/epoch-rollforward.md; perf run artifacts: artifacts/334210/benchmarks.html.
